subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the non-full registration guard is fixed, should OpenClaw accept `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`/`node-pty` native package ownership and the upstream MXC SDK argv-carried `--config-base64` sandbox config boundary for this prerelease Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: This choice involves native sandbox executables, an install-script dependency, and process-argv visibility for sandbox policy; automation can identify and narrow the boundary but cannot set OpenClaw's security acceptance threshold.

options.title: Accept After Guard
options.body: Fix the registration-mode side effect, then have an admin/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport before merge.

options.title: Pause For Upstream Transport
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer merge until MXC SDK provides a non-argv config transport or stronger policy secrecy story.

options.title: Decline First-Party Package
options.body: Close or redirect the backend outside first-party OpenClaw packaging if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own this sandbox dependency boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept After Guard
recommendation.body: Fix the registration-mode side effect, then have an admin/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They made the latest concrete parity and acceptance request on this PR and are already requested for review.
